quote: ’Tis early practice only makes the master.
source: Friedrich Schiller, Wilhelm Tell, Act III, scene 1, to Hedwig (Tell) (trans. Theodore Martin, 1847)
speaker: Wilhelm Tell

evidence.where: Archive.org OCR of Bohn’s Standard Library, Schiller’s Works, Historical and Dramatic, vol. 2 (1872 Bell and Daldy reprint), page 496: Tell. ’Tis early practice only makes the master. Bohn’s preface, dated York Street, November 1846, states Wilhelm Tell is translated by Theodore Martin, Esq.; contents give Tell at pages 449 to 563. The Online Books Page lists the first printing as London: H. G. Bohn, 1847. Cross-checked with Project Gutenberg ebook 6788, which names Martin.
evidence.edition: The Works of Frederick Schiller, vol. 2: Revolt of the Netherlands continued, Wallenstein and Wilhelm Tell (London: Henry G. Bohn, Bohn’s Standard Library, 1847)
evidence.locator: Wilhelm Tell, Act III, scene 1, p. 496, Tell’s reply to Hedwig’s The boys begin to use the bow betimes (German: Früh übt sich, was ein Meister werden will)

reason: The line is verbatim in the Bohn volume, whose preface names Theodore Martin as translator of Tell, and in the Gutenberg text. The proposer’s unconfirmed c. 1847 is now settled: preface November 1846, volume dated 1847. Martin was not yet knighted, so the source drops Sir. Not shipped; Schiller has no line in the year.
